Key responsibilities

• Recruits, trains, mentors, and manages a high-performing key account team.

• Sets clear sales targets and KPIs for the team and drives performance to deliver targets.

• Prepares, participate, and conducts regular account reviews/performance evaluations, providing feedback and coaching.

• Cultivates empowered account team, leveraging digital tools, foster a culture of continuous learning, an environment of excellence, leading through inspiration.

• P and L ownership for account and focused strategic (multi-year) outlook on how to grow joint profit pool with customer, leveraging 360 levers.

• Drives yearly negotiation, resolving issues with customers and meeting sales objectives.

• Leads the relationship with buyer on account / banner level.

• Directly involved in day-to-day interactions with senior stakeholders from account/banner.

• Provides on-going support to key accounts ensuring they receive high-quality customer service.

• Serve as the lead point of contact for key account management matters, responsible for trade-to-trade preparation and engagement, developing long term strategic customer relationships

• Forecast quarterly and annual account projections enhancing accuracy with use of commercial platform AI/ML models.

• Monitors and reports on key account performance metrics to senior leadership, building gap fill and corrective action plans.

• Analyses key account preferences and data to identify growth opportunities, employing AI and ML tools for predictive analytics and competitor dynamics.

• Provides insights to the marketing team to enhance product positioning, assortment, mix and promotional optimization.

Are you passionate about driving GCP compliance and quality excellence across global clinical development programs?

If so, now is your chance to join Ascendis Pharma as our new Associate Director, GCP Quality.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs in our Endocrinology Rare Disease and Oncology portfolios. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a passionate Associate Director, GCP Quality to join our growing team. As a key member of the Ascendis Pharma team, you will play a crucial role in performing GCP audits. This is an exciting opportunity to work in a fast-paced environment, collaborate with cross-functional, global teams working together to achieve extraordinary results.

You will be joining the GCP Quality team consisting of 4 colleagues, and report directly to Lone Neergaard Pedersen, Senior Director & QP, Head of GCP Quality who is based in Hellerup_._ You will be based in Hellerup.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Plan, perform, and report GCP audits (internal, clinical trial sites and service provider audits)

• Review and analyze audit, inspection, deviation and CAPA data to identify root cause, compliance trends and areas of exposure related to GCP

• Review and approve quality intakes, serious breach reporting, deviations and CAPAs

• Provide expert compliance and regulatory advice within GCP

• Author and maintain procedures owned by GCP Quality

• Support regulatory intelligence monitoring and assessing impact as well as implementation of new/updated GCP regulation

• Lead and support the planning, conduct and follow-up on regulatory inspections

• Collaborate with subject matter experts to formulate responses to GCP relevant inspection findings

• Drive quality development initiatives within the GCP area

• Perform expert consultation on complex aspects of GCP to projects teams and departments

• Perform the role of quality partner to assigned departments

Qualifications and Skills:

You hold a relevant academic degree - preferably a master's degree in life sciences - and at least 8 years of experience within GCP quality from the pharmaceutical industry. You are proficient in English at a professional level, both written and spoken.

Furthermore, you have:

• Demonstrated experience as a lead GCP auditor of clinical trial sites and service providers

• Strong working knowledge of drug development, clinical operations, regulatory authorities, and/or quality assurance

• Demonstrated proficiency in English at a professional level, both written and spoken

• Obtained a lead auditor certification

Key competencies:

You are a strong team player with excellent stakeholder management skills and a proactive, solution-oriented mindset. You thrive in a dynamic environment and can balance business needs with quality and compliance requirements.

You are highly structured, analytical, and able to simplify complex issues into clear recommendations and actions. You communicate confidently and effectively with stakeholders across a global organization and build strong relationships based on trust, integrity, and collaboration.

Travel: 30-50 days per year.

Office: Tuborg Boulevard 12, 2900 Hellerup, Denmark

Apply now.

We evaluate applications when received, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Please note that we conduct interviews on a rolling basis and reserve the right to remove the job posting at any time.

To ensure your application is reviewed, please submit it through the specified platform - applications sent by email or other channels will not be evaluated.

For more details about the position or the company, please contact Lone Neergaard Pedersen, Senior Director & QP, Head of GCP Quality, lnp@ascendispharma.com

You can learn more about Ascendis by visiting our website www.ascendispharma.com

Applications must be submitted in English and will be treated confidentially.

A note to recruiters:

We do not allow external search party solicitation.  Presentation of candidates without written permission from the Ascendis Pharma HR team (specifically from: Talent Acquisition Partner or Human Resources Director) is not allowed.  If this occurs, your ownership of these candidates will not be acknowledged.

We are looking for a Payroll Specialist who can ensure stable, accurate, and professional payroll processes, and who thrives in a collaborative environment with a focus on quality and continuous improvement

About the job

As our new Payroll Specialist, you will become part of Group Finance, where you will join a larger team while sharing the primary responsibility for payroll accounting with one colleague. You will primarily be responsible for Danish payroll, and you will also provide support related to international payroll processes in our sales countries, where payroll administration is primarily handled by external payroll providers.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Managing the payroll process from A to Z, from data collection and validation to payment and reconciliation

• Payroll controls, including validation, quality assurance, and the handling of alerts and reports

• Administration of new hires, terminations, absences, holiday accounts, reimbursements, and related payroll activities

• Handling severance payments, holiday pay accruals, and other payroll-related accounting entries

• Payroll reconciliations, including three-way reconciliations between the payroll system, finance, and statutory reporting/eIncome, as well as reconciliations of accrued and outstanding payroll-related balances

• Preparing audit documentation and delivering ad hoc reporting

• Contributing to process optimization and continuous improvement initiatives, including ensuring best practices across payroll processes

You will report to the Director, Group Finance, while working closely with HR Operations.

Who are you?

We are looking for someone who has:

• Experience with payroll systems (SAP Payroll and SAP SuccessFactors are considered an advantage)

• Strong Excel skills and a solid understanding of systems in general. You are comfortable working analytically with large datasets, identifying patterns and connections in data, and applying a strong technical understanding

• A keen eye for detail and a high degree of data accuracy

• Knowledge of payroll legislation and, ideally, collective agreements for blue collar employees

• Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate professionally with HR, Finance, and employees across the organization, including responding to payroll-related inquiries from employees

• The ability to work independently and take ownership of your responsibilities, while also enjoying close collaboration with a colleague on shared tasks

• A proactive and curious approach to processes, along with a desire to contribute to continuous improvements

• The ability to work in a structured and reliable manner, as our payroll processes require a high level of accuracy and quality

• Fluency in Danish and strong English language skills

Who are we?

In Group Finance, you will become part of a dedicated team focused on quality, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving. In addition to Payroll, the department includes Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Cash and Bank Management, Controlling, as well as process owners and system specialists who work closely together across Finance and other key functions.

The team has an informal and supportive culture, deep professional expertise, and a strong commitment to helping one another while continuously developing and improving processes together.

Why should you join Orifarm?

At Orifarm, we are 2,300 employees united by a shared purpose: improving access to affordable medicine for the people who need it. Founded in Odense, Denmark in 1994 by Birgitte & Hans Bøgh-Sørensen, we have built our business on challenging conventional thinking to make affordable high-quality pharmaceuticals more accessible across Europe. Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We live by the mindset Challenge Accepted. It reflects our explorer spirit and can-do attitude, where challenges are perceived as opportunities. We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. We offer autonomy and great opportunities for career advancement, enabling our employees to shape their professional development. We value flexibility and provide a hybrid work model with the possibility of working from home two days a week.

We invite you to join Orifarm, if you are curious, ambitious, and accept the challenge of making affordable healthcare accessible.

We encourage everyone to apply

At Orifarm, we welcome people from all backgrounds, recognizing that the best outcomes come from a diverse and inclusive work environment. Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

Are you passionate about developing advanced microwave oscillator systems for world-class Doppler radar solutions?

At Weibel, you will become part of a growing, technology-driven company where curiosity, innovation, and dedication are the foundation of our global success. We develop and manufacture high-performance radar systems at our in-house production facilities, enabling us to explore new solutions while maintaining uncompromising quality. Our greatest asset is our talented employees, who work in a modern environment and continuously advance our market-leading radar solutions for applications such as air surveillance and precision tracking.

We are strengthening our Antenna R&D Group and are looking for a Senior Microwave Engineer to join us as we enter a new growth phase.

About the position

As our new colleague, you will drive the development of microwave oscillators from early concept through design, integration, and deployment into our radar systems. You will collaborate closely with colleagues across analog, digital, and mechanical engineering disciplines. In addition, you will contribute to architectural improvements in collaboration with our system architects.

Your primary responsibilities include:

• Designing, developing, and optimizing oscillator modules and circuitry for high-performance radar applications.

• Researching and evaluating new oscillator technologies to improve phase noise, frequency stability, and overall system performance.

• Serving as the technical subject-matter expert for oscillator designs and their integration.

• Supporting prototype assembly, testing, and DFM reviews to ensure successful transfer to production.

• Providing technical support to in-house production and customers through engineering guidance, root-cause analysis, and documentation.

This is an exciting opportunity to shape the frequency-generation foundation of Weibel's radar portfolio and enhance the performance of our next-generation radar systems.

About you

You thrive in an Agile environment, where you work both independently and in close collaboration with your team and cross-functional stakeholders. You value continuous learning and are comfortable operating in a dynamic R&D setting with multiple parallel activities, some requiring immediate attention and others progressing through structured project plans.

Your qualifications include:

• An M.Sc. or PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field, preferably with a specialization in RF or microwave hardware design.

• Hands-on experience with oscillator and frequency-generation design, e.g., VCOs, DROs, or PLL-based synthesizers, including optimization of phase noise, frequency stability, and spectral purity.

• A strong background in RF, microwave, or mixed-signal systems development, combined with a solid understanding of the full product development lifecycle.

• Familiarity with regulatory requirements (e.g., radio and EMC) and military standards applied in mission-critical industries.

• Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

Furthermore, you are comfortable leveraging AI-assisted tools to improve engineering efficiency and quality.

Your new team

Our team consists of over 10 engaged colleagues, with experience ranging from a few years to more than 35 years in radar engineering. The team is part of our cross-functional Antenna R&D Group, bringing together architects and design specialists across RF, analog, digital, and mechanical domains to deliver cutting-edge radar technology.

Contact and application

Please submit your application via our website using the “Apply” button. If you have any questions about the position, you are very welcome to contact Engineering Manager, Adin Kanlic, at adk@weibel.dk.

The application deadline is 16 November.

Please note that we review applications on an ongoing basis.

Employment in this role is subject to the ability to provide a clean criminal record and to obtain the required security clearance.

We look forward to receiving your application.

Become part of a Danish company

Weibel Scientific A/S is a Danish-owned engineering company experiencing strong growth. We develop and manufacture high‑technology radar systems for use in areas such as space research, aviation, defense, and the protection of critical infrastructure. We are a world leader in the development of Doppler radars and, since our establishment in 1977, we have delivered more than 4,500 state‑of‑the-art radar systems to over 40 countries.

Our headquarters are located in Allerød and employ nearly 600 people.

At Weibel, you can look forward to an exciting and challenging position in a dynamic and forward‑looking company with in‑house production and advanced technological development.

Read more about us on our website.

Do you have experience with planning and testing complex systems?

At Weibel you will join a truly technology driven company that delivers excellent Doppler Radars across the world. Weibel is recognized as a world-leader in radar technology, with our radars performing with a precision largely unmatched by competitors. Applications for our radars include Space Research, Missile Defence, Instrumentation Systems and lately for drone and UAS detection. Our radars are produced at our HQ in Allerød, north of Copenhagen.

Increasing customer demand means that the company is experiencing rapid growth. As part of this, we are extending our leadership team in our System Integration, Test & Verification team with one more experienced System Test Manager.

Oversee the system test of our state-of-the-art radars

As System Test Manager you take ownership of system test activities across the development lifecycle of our advanced radar products. In this leadership role you will plan, prioritize, and drive the work of one or maybe a few Scrum teams of test engineers, ensuring that integrated hardware and software meet system requirements, performance targets, quality standards, and customer expectations.

You will be part of a test leadership team comprising four System Test Managers. Each manager supports a dedicated program with deliveries based on our radar platforms and owns the test plan for the projects in the program. Coordination with the other three test managers is therefore also relevant to inspire and maximize reuse to continuously improve testing and execute as efficiently as possible.

Key responsibilities:

• Plan and drive the execution of integration, functional, performance, robustness, environmental and regression testing through one or more Scrum teams of test engineers.

• Define test scope and methods and translate program priorities and test needs into clear team objectives, backlogs, milestones, dependencies, and delivery expectations.

• Align with the other System Test Managers on shared methods, mechanisms and specialist resources.

• Establish test readiness criteria, and communicate product maturity, coverage, results, and residual risks to the Technical Project Manager in the Program

• Drive automation, repeatability, data quality, and continuous improvement in test processes.

• Support customer demonstrations, qualification activities, and formal acceptance testing when required.

• Act as a technical lead and mentor for a team of System Test Engineers, and be part of creating a culture with focus on quality and continuous improvement

• Collaborate with Mechanical, Hardware and Software development teams to define test requirements and ensure seamless integration

• Ensure compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements

About you

You thrive in an environment that requires you to work independently on some tasks and in close collaboration with your colleagues across the entire company on others. You have excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with a detailed-oriented mindset. You show initiative and drive, take responsibility, have strong communication skills, work effectively across teams and dare to challenge the team to ensure high quality. You understand how the Scrum methodology applies in a system test context.

Your CV include:

• A relevant engineering degree

• 10+ years of experience in system testing of complex integrated HW and SW systems

• Proven technical leadership experience, managing test teams in an agile development environment

• Experience working with Requirements and Test management tools (we use Helix)

• Strong understanding of test automation tools, frameworks, and methodologies

• Experience with systems engineering in relation to complex systems

• Relevant certifications (e.g. ISTQB) is an advantage

• Fluent in English both written and spoken

• Experience with radar systems or complex systems for military use, is considered an advantage

Your new team

You will be joining our team of more than 25 colleagues in the Integration, Test & Verification team. Our responsibilities span across system integration and testing as well as qualification of our products and we are divided into two competency domains. Each domain is represented by an Engineering Manager in the Test Leadership team, which also has four System Test Managers, where you will be one.

The level of experience in the team spans from newly graduates to more than +20 years of experience. Our team members have different educational backgrounds that vary from satellite, aerospace, earth and space physics to mechanical and electrical engineering. We have created it in this way, because we believe that bringing people with different competences together will generate the best solutions.

Contact and application

Please apply at our website using the ”Apply” button. If you have any questions, you are very welcome to contact Director Integration, Test & Verification, Lars Boye on lrb@weibel.dk.

The deadline is the 22nd of November 2026.

Please be aware that it is a requirement for this position that you can provide a criminal record with no remarks and obtain a security clearance.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Become part of a Danish company

Weibel Scientific A/S is a Danish-owned engineering company experiencing strong growth. We develop and manufacture high‑technology radar systems for use in areas such as space research, aviation, defense, and the protection of critical infrastructure. We are a world leader in the development of Doppler radars and, since our establishment in 1977, we have delivered more than 4,500 state‑of‑the‑art radar systems to over 40 countries.

Our headquarters are located in Allerød and employ nearly 600 people.

At Weibel, you can look forward to an exciting and challenging position in a dynamic and forward‑looking company with in-house production and advanced technological development.

Read more about us on our website.

**The Impact You'll Make

**As a Production Engineer at Danfoss Silkeborg in our plastic moulding department, you will play a key role in developing, maintaining, and improving our plastic injection moulding processes that produce plastic components for some of Danfoss' most iconic products - the radiator thermostats and its valve - made right here in Silkeborg.

You will be instrumental in ensuring that our plastic injection moulding processes remain capable, reliable, and ready to meet future customer demands.

You will work alongside a team of 11 skilled Production Engineers, where you will take part of the ownership of our plastic injection moulding processes and related production equipment. Working closely with operators, tool technicians, maintenance, quality, and product development teams, you will drive process optimization, troubleshoot complex production challenges, validate new products and materials, and implement robust solutions that ensure stable and efficient production.

This role offers the opportunity to combine hands-on engineering, problem-solving, and continuous improvement in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where new technologies, products, and materials are continuously introduced and your will have a direct impact on product quality, process capability, equipment uptime and productivity.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**You'll work closely with operators, tool technicians, maintenance specialists, quality engineers, and product development teams to improve process performance and support the introduction of new products, materials, and technologies.

**You Will

**

• Own and continuously improve plastic injection moulding processes, ensuring safe, stable, and efficient production performance

• Optimize moulding parameters, cycle times, material utilization, and process capability to increase productivity, capacity, and reduce waste

• Lead troubleshooting and root cause analysis of process deviations, quality issues, scrap, and equipment downtime, implementing sustainable solutions

• Introduce and validate new products, materials, tooling, and equipment, ensuring smooth implementation and integration into production

• Strengthen process and quality control through structured methods such as APQP, process validation, PFMEAs, control plans, and maintenance strategies

**What We're Looking For

**To succeed in this role, you'll combine technical expertise with a practical, hands-on approach to solving manufacturing challenges.

**Essential Qualifications

**

• Technical background within plastic processing, injection moulding, production engineering, mechanical engineering, toolmaking, polymer engineering, or a related field

• Strong understanding of injection moulding processes, tooling, polymer materials, and production optimization

• Ability to combine analytical thinking with practical problem-solving on the shop floor

• Strong collaboration and communication skills, with a proactive and solution-oriented mindset when working across functions and with external partners

• Fluency in Danish and English, both written and spoken

Experience with APQP, PFMEA, process validation, continuous improvement methodologies, or quality management systems will be considered an advantage.

**What You'll Get From Us

**At Danfoss, you'll join an experienced and collaborative engineering environment where you'll have the opportunity to influence products manufactured in high volumes and used in homes around the world.

You'll work with advanced injection moulding technologies and play a key role in introducing new products, materials, and manufacturing solutions, while being supported by knowledgeable colleagues who value teamwork, technical excellence, and continuous improvement.

We promote from within and support your learning with mentoring, training, and access to global opportunities.

You’ll have flexibility, autonomy, and support to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment where people of all backgrounds are respected, and valued for who they are.

You’ll receive benefits like annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, personal insurance, and more. These vary by country and contract, but they’re worth asking about—we think they’re pretty great.

**Ready to Make a Difference?

**If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you!

Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

For information about the recruitment process, please contact Talent Acquisition Partner, Gerd Veierskov, +45 3057 1882

**Our Commitment to Transparency

**Salary ranges listed reflect only primary location and currency. For local salary ranges and specific benefits in your preferred hiring location, please ask your Talent Acquisition representative for more information.

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our **FAQ Page.

**All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

Marketing Coordinator Global Marketing

Looking for an opportunity to coordinate global marketing initiatives across markets, channels, and stakeholders in a fast-growing MedTech company?

At Qufora, our mission is to improve the quality of life for people living with chronic bowel disorders through intuitive, life-changing bowel management solutions. We strive to create a supportive and rewarding work environment.

As a result of an internal career move, we are looking for a Marketing Coordinator to join our Global Marketing team. This is a highly visible role where you will work across campaigns, digital channels, localisation, events, and marketing operations to help ensure our global marketing initiatives are delivered effectively across markets.

If you enjoy creating structure, coordinating with stakeholders, maintaining high-quality marketing assets, and making things happen, then this could be the role for you.

Qufora HQ is located north of Copenhagen in Allerød. We currently employ around 75 people in Headquarters, and we work with our 5 subsidiaries and 16 distributors across the globe.

Your role

As Marketing Coordinator in Global Marketing you’ll be the operational engine behind the implementation of our global marketing activities. Working across campaigns, localisation, digital platforms, and cross-functional projects, you will help ensure that marketing initiatives are ready for market and successfully deployed across local markets and centrally managed channels.

What success looks like

To succeed in this role, you’ll enjoy creating structure, coordinating with multiple stakeholders, managing marketing assets and processes, and turning global plans into market-ready materials and activities across markets and channels.

You combine strong operational discipline with sound judgement and are comfortable working with marketing materials, content, and digital platforms. You naturally spot what needs updating, what is missing, and where additional coordination is needed to keep things moving forward.

**What you’ll be responsible for

**

• Enabling the effective execution of global marketing campaigns, content and activities across markets and channels

• Coordinating localisation and ensuring global marketing assets are localised, approved and execution-ready

• Maintaining marketing assets, platforms, and processes to ensure content remain up to date, accessible, and ready for use across markets and channels

• Supporting the operation and maintenance of key digital platforms, websites, and marketing channels

• Coordinating with stakeholders, projects, and external partners to ensure effective delivery of marketing activities

Who we’re looking for

We imagine you are a highly organised and proactive marketing professional who enjoys turning plans into action. You are comfortable managing multiple priorities simultaneously and enjoy working with different stakeholders across functions and countries.

**You bring

**

• 5 – 7 years of experience in marketing, coordination, project management, communications, or a related field, which might be from a medical device company, or an industry with similar dynamics – but not a requirement

• Experience working with digital platforms and content management systems

• Strong project coordination and organisational skills

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English

• A structured and detail-oriented mindset

• Curiosity about new tools and technologies, including AI

**Who you are

**

• A natural coordinator who enjoys creating clarity and structure

• A hands-on doer who follows through and gets things done

• Comfortable working with both people, processes, and content

• Service-minded and collaborative

• Curious, resourceful, and continuously looking for better ways of working

Why join Qufora?

At Qufora, we are driven by a simple purpose: helping people with chronic bowel disorders live a better life.

You’ll join a broad cross-functional commercial team of around 20 colleagues spanning Global Marketing & Product Management, Customer Programs, Strategy, and Distributor Sales, giving you exposure to many different aspects of the business and the opportunity to play a central role in the implementation of global marketing initiatives.

Our culture is built on trust, openness, collaboration, and a strong customer focus. With a flat organisational structure and an agile way of working, you’ll find an environment where ideas are heard, decisions are made quickly, and colleagues are encouraged to take ownership, grow, and develop.

For someone who enjoys variety, responsibility, and coordinating the many elements required to deliver marketing activities across markets and centrally managed channels, this role offers the opportunity to work across campaigns, localisation, digital channels, events and marketing operations while building broad experience within global marketing in MedTech.

Interested in joining Qufora?

Submit your application via LinkedIn. We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis, and we look forward to hearing from you.

Are you passionate about renewable energy and eager to work at the forefront of the global energy transition? PEAK Wind is seeking an AI Engineer to help shape our AI roadmap and to build and orchestrate the agents our colleagues and clients will use every day. At PEAK Wind, AI is moving from prototypes into production, and renewable energy operations produce exactly the kind of complex, high-volume data where AI can deliver significant value.

Introducing the Data & Intelligence Team

You will become part of our Data & Intelligence (D&I) team, where we work within PEAK Wind’s asset management service offering and manage full value chain data management for our clients. We support renewable energy assets worldwide through data management, reporting solutions, analytics, and AI capabilities, helping deliver data-driven solutions that support our clients and renewable energy projects. Our team consists of highly motivated professionals who bring diverse backgrounds and a strong commitment to excellence. We support one another, share knowledge, and celebrate both individual and collective achievements.

You will report to the Head of Data & Intelligence and work day-to-day with our small team of engineers who have been building internal AI products at PEAK Wind for several years. You will work closely with colleagues across different areas, bringing your perspective to a collaborative and purposeful team environment.

How You Will Make an Impact

As an AI Engineer, you will take AI solutions from idea to production and keep them there. You will co-own our AI roadmap: helping decide which agents we build, in what order, and what “working” means for each of them. Then you will build them.

Our agent portfolio serves two audiences. Internally, our agents give colleagues across PEAK Wind a well-governed way to work with company knowledge, generate reports, and analyse wind farm performance. Other internal agents help our own engineers specify and build new features faster. Externally, we provide agent-driven capabilities in our client-facing products.

On smaller initiatives you may be the engineer primarily responsible for taking the solution from first conversation to deployment. On larger initiatives, you will work closely with Product Owners, data engineers, and domain experts in asset management. Either way, the distance from an idea to something running is deliberately short. Your key responsibilities will include:

• Co-develop and maintain the PEAK Wind AI roadmap with the AI team, turning business needs into scoped, sequenced deliverables

• Design, build, and deploy agentic systems for internal colleagues, from reporting and wind farm analysis to engineering-productivity agents

• Design, build, and deploy AI-driven features and agents in our client-facing products, working with SCADA, operations, and asset management data

• Orchestrate multi-agent workflows: tool use, memory, retrieval over company and client data, and integration with our platform through APIs

• Build the evaluation systems that tell us whether an agent works, before and after it reaches production

• Own the data and infrastructure work behind your own agents on the cloud.

• Implement responsible-AI practices for operational energy data: access control, data isolation between clients, logging, and guardrails

• Ship early and iterate put prototypes in users’ hands fast and feed what you learn back into the roadmap

• Collaborate with Product Owners and stakeholders to understand what they need, and push back when AI is not the right tool

• Document what you build so others can maintain, extend, and trust it

What Will Make You Successful in This Role

At PEAK Wind, we know success comes in many forms. What matters most is your mindset, curiosity, and drive to make an impact. The following qualities and experiences will help you succeed in this role:

• A degree in a relevant field such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or similar, or an equivalent track record of shipping software

• Hands-on experience in software development, ML, data engineering, or AI Engineering, including AI applications you have helped take into production

• Strong Python and/or TypeScript, and hands-on experience with at least one agent framework

• Experience building or extending evals for LLM and agent behaviour, or an interest in developing deeper expertise in this area

• Experience building in cloud environments, preferably Microsoft Azure; familiarity with PostgreSQL, APIs, and modern web stacks is an advantage

• You code with AI tools such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor as a matter of course

• Professional experience in the energy industry or another complex technical environment; renewable energy or SCADA experience is an advantage but not required

• Clear and effective communication skills in English, both spoken and written, with technical and non-technical stakeholders alike

• A go-doer mentality: you would rather ship something real this week and improve it next week than perfect it in a document

• A structured approach to problem-solving and the ability to take initiative, including owning a product from idea to delivery

• The ability to stay calm and constructive in a high-paced environment

• A collaborative mindset and the ability to thrive in an international, cross-functional team

This role is designed for an engineer who has already gained some hands-on experience building AI solutions and is now looking to deepen that expertise in a highly practical, production-focused environment and enjoys building and learning.

Why Join PEAK Wind

• A real mandate to build with AI: an existing roadmap, internal users who want what you build, and clients ready to adopt it

• An international, inclusive, and diverse workplace where differences are valued

• The opportunity to work on leading renewable energy projects alongside experienced industry professionals

• Flexible working arrangements that support both your career and personal life

• A flat organisational structure where your ideas are welcomed and your contributions matter

• A strong focus on your learning, development, and professional growth

• A culture that values commitment, meaningful contributions, and having fun

Our Commitment to Inclusion and Fair Hiring

We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace drives innovation, creativity, and stronger results. At PEAK Wind, we are committed to fair and transparent hiring processes, welcoming candidates from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Our hiring decisions focus on what each person brings to the role and our team, and we are committed to ensuring transparent salary structures, with pay decisions based on clear, objective, and gender‑neutral criteria. Salary information, including the relevant salary band, will be shared with candidates when they are invited to a first interview.

How to Apply

We look forward to receiving your application. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the recruitment process once the right candidate has been found. Please apply directly through our website. If you have any questions or would like to know more about the position, please contact People & Development at recruitment@peak-wind.com.

About PEAK Wind

PEAK Wind is an independent renewable energy specialist in commercial, financial, and technical operations, delivering advisory, intelligence, and asset management services to investors and developers around the world. From onshore and offshore wind generation to Power-to-X, we work across the entire energy lifecycle to optimise operations and maintenance, enhance asset performance, and provide a holistic view of renewable infrastructure portfolios.

Our values - Expertise, Passion, Unity, and Integrity - are reflected in everything we do, from how we support our clients to how we collaborate as a team. At PEAK Wind, you will be able to apply your professional skills in a dynamic environment and experience a meaningful responsibility and involvement.

Are you passionate about regulatory affairs and bringing innovative vaccines to patients worldwide? Would you like to shape global CMC strategies and support the expansion of our life-saving vaccines?

Then you could be our next Regulatory Affairs CMC Manager.

At Bavarian Nordic, we are committed to saving and improving lives by unlocking the power of the immune system. Our commercial product portfolio includes market-leading vaccines against smallpox, mpox, rabies, tick-borne encephalitis, typhoid fever, cholera, and chikungunya. We excel in R&D innovation, manufacturing, and commercialization, striving to improve people's health and quality of life worldwide while protecting our tomorrow.

**The role

**Your primary focus will be the continued global expansion of our chikungunya vaccine following its initial approvals in the US and Europe. You will play an important role in shaping the regulatory approach for new markets and supporting the vaccine throughout its lifecycle.

Working across R&D and Global Operations, you will provide clear regulatory direction, coordinate activities across functions, and help move complex regulatory priorities forward.

As Regulatory Affairs CMC Manager, you will join a skilled team of three colleagues responsible for global CMC regulatory activities. Based in Kvistgaard, you will report to the Senior Manager, Regulatory Affairs CMC. Occasional travel should be expected.

**Your Key Responsibilities

**

• Lead regulatory CMC strategies and submissions that enable our vaccines to be registered and launched in new countries worldwide

• Prepare and maintain high-quality scientific and regulatory documentation to support submissions to health authorities

• Act as a trusted regulatory partner to cross-functional teams, providing guidance on regulatory requirements and submission expectations

• Manage interactions together with the Global Regulatory Lead with global health authorities, including preparation of briefing materials and responses to regulatory questions

• Drive regulatory activities throughout the product lifecycle, ensuring that manufacturing, process, or product changes are effectively implemented and approved in global markets

**What We Are Looking For

**You hold an MSc or PhD in a scientific discipline such as Pharmacy, Biotechnology, Chemistry, Biology, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field.

In addition, you bring:

• Approximately 8+ years of experience in Regulatory Affairs within the pharmaceutical, biotech, or vaccine industry

• Strong experience with global regulatory submissions and international health authorities

• Experience with CMC regulatory activities for biologics, vaccines, or complex pharmaceutical products

• Solid understanding of pharmaceutical development, manufacturing, and regulatory requirements

• Excellent scientific writing and authoring skills

• Strong project management and planning capabilities

• Fluency in written and spoken English

**Who You Are

**To succeed in this role, you are:

• A collaborative team player who enjoys working across functions and cultures

• Detail-oriented and able to manage complex documentation with a high level of accuracy

• Proactive, agile, and comfortable navigating changing priorities

• A strong stakeholder manager who can build trusted relationships across the organization

• Curious, solution-oriented, and motivated by making a global impact

**What We Offer

**You will join an international vaccine company with unique technology, dedicated colleagues, and a collaborative culture built on teamwork, openness, and scientific excellence.

We offer a flexible work environment, opportunities for professional development, and the chance to contribute to work with a meaningful global impact.

**Caught your interest?

**If you are ready to shape global regulatory strategies and help bring innovative vaccines to more patients worldwide, apply through our designated application platform. Applications submitted by email will not be considered.

Please note that visa sponsorship and relocation assistance are not available for this position.

_Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

jobs.occupation: Executive Director Partnerships, Advocacy, Engagement & Resource Mobilisation
jobs.description:
Would you like to shape how one of the world’s leading humanitarian organisations builds partnerships, and mobilises resources needed to support people affected by displacement?

This is an opportunity to bring your leadership, external engagement and resource mobilisation experience to a mission with human impact. As Executive Director for Partnerships, Advocacy, Engagement & Resource Mobilisation (PAER) at the Danish Refugee Council (DRC), you will strengthen DRC’s voice, relationships and funding base - positioning DRC as a trusted partner and advocate for displaced people.

You will join DRC at an important time for the humanitarian sector, as needs continue to rise while funding and humanitarian space are under increasing pressure. As a member of the Executive Management Team, you will help set DRC’s strategic direction and lead a broad global portfolio spanning strategic partnerships, institutional and private fundraising, advocacy, external communications, press, international representations, and asylum and refugee rights.

**About The Job

**Reporting to the Secretary General, you will set direction for DRC’s global partnerships, advocacy, engagement and resource mobilisation agenda. Working closely with the Executive Management Team, country leadership, and senior functional leaders, you will expand high-level relationships with institutional donors, global foundations, private contributors, private-sector partners to secure more sustainable and flexible funding.

You will harness DRC’s global advocacy, communications and press efforts across countries, regions, representations and headquarters, strengthening DRC’s position as a relevant influencing and dialogue partner for donors, political stakeholders, peers and the wider humanitarian system. You will also oversee DRC’s representations in Geneva, Brussels and Berlin, as well as our representative presence in London, and provide leadership for the Asylum & Refugee Rights department and its specialised expertise in asylum procedures, refugee rights and legal aid.

You will lead and develop leaders across the PAER portfolio, foster collaboration across the organisation, and ensure sound people planning, employee well-being and financial management. Based at DRC’s headquarters in Copenhagen, you will represent DRC internally and externally, communicate its priorities with clarity and build trusted relationships across cultures, sectors and geographies.

The impact you will make:

• Shape DRC’s global strategy and PAER agenda as a member of the Executive Management Team, helping translate organisational priorities into coordinated action.

• Expand institutional and private partnerships to secure more sustainable and flexible funding for DRC’s humanitarian mission.

• Strengthen DRC’s global advocacy, communications and influence on displacement-related agendas with donors, policymakers and humanitarian partners.

• Lead DRC’s international representations with a focus on external relations, and its asylum and refugee rights portfolio, connecting specialist expertise with global engagement.

• Develop senior leaders and promote effective collaboration, people management and financial stewardship across the PAER portfolio.

**About You

**You are a purpose-driven executive who combines political judgement, entrepreneurial energy and strong relationship-building skills. You understand the global humanitarian and development landscape and can translate opportunities into lasting partnerships, influence and income. You are an inclusive, inspiring and empowering leader with the ability to create momentum across a complex international organisation.

What you will bring:

• Senior-level experience building institutional and private partnerships in the international humanitarian or development sector.

• Deep knowledge of humanitarian funding to forced displacement and related global policy priorities.

• A proven record in resource mobilisation, high-level advocacy, external engagement and policy dialogue.

• Political acumen and credibility with senior government, donor, foundation and private-sector stakeholders.

• Executive leadership experience and an inclusive, entrepreneurial and high-integrity leadership style.

All employees in DRC should master DRC's core competencies: Communicating, Taking the lead, Collaborating, Striving for excellence and Demonstrating integrity.

**We offer

**Contract length: Permanent

Work location:  Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken station

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and Lederaftalen between Dansk Arbejdsgiverforening and Lederne (agreement for managers), which can be found here: www.lederne.dk. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.

We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit.

**Application process

**If you are motivated by the opportunity to strengthen a global humanitarian organisation through partnerships, advocacy, engagement and resource mobilisation, we would welcome your application. Korn Ferry is assisting the Danish Refugee Council with the recruitment of the Executive Director, Partnerships, Advocacy, Engagement & Resource Mobilisation. Please submit your motivated application and CV through the designated recruitment channel.

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English.. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

Closing date for applications: 5th November 2026

Further information For questions regarding the vacancy please contact: Georgie Horn, Senior Associate Korn Ferry: DRC_PAER@KornFerry.com

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website drc.ngo .

Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.

On-call Waiters & Bartenders - Bring your personality to Hobo Copenhagen

A warm hello. A thoughtful recommendation. Noticing when someone could use a hand. Great hospitality starts with small moments, and we’re looking for people who enjoy creating them.

We’re looking for on-call waiters and bartenders to join our F&B team at Hobo Copenhagen, helping out across our cocktailbar, all-day bar & café, restaurant and breakfast service.

You might already have some hospitality experience, or you might be looking for your first opportunity in the industry. What matters most is your personality, reliability and willingness to learn. Bring your curiosity and energy, and we’ll help you build your skills.

Find your feet with us

You’ll work alongside experienced colleagues who will show you the ropes and support you during service. Depending on your experience and interests, you’ll:

• 
Welcome guests and help them feel comfortable from the moment they arrive.

• 
Serve food and drinks, learning about our menus so you can share favourites and make recommendations with confidence.

• 
Support service behind the bar, preparing drinks and keeping the bar ready for the next round.

• 
Help prepare for service, set tables and keep our spaces welcoming throughout the shift.

• 
Stay attentive to guests, listen to their requests and ask a colleague whenever you need a hand.

• 
Support the team with clearing, resetting and the everyday details that keep service flowing.

You don’t need to be equally experienced on the floor and behind the bar. Tell us what you enjoy and where you feel confident, and we’ll explore where you fit best.

What you bring

You enjoy meeting people and are happy to let your personality show. You’re curious, approachable and willing to get involved, even when something is new to you.

You take your commitments seriously, arrive ready for your shift and support your colleagues when things get busy. You’re comfortable asking questions and taking feedback as you learn.

You can communicate with guests and colleagues in English. Experience from a restaurant, café or bar is welcome, and being comfortable working both on the floor and behind the bar is a definite plus.

You should be available to work at least every other weekend. Being able and keen to work more is a welcome plus. Shifts can be in the morning, daytime or evening.

What you’ll be part of

At Hobo, we bring a professional, passionate and playful approach to hospitality. We care about good service and want people to feel comfortable being themselves, both as guests and as colleagues.

You’ll join a new team during our opening journey, with hands-on training, supportive colleagues and the chance to grow in confidence as you gain experience.

Hobo Copenhagen is part of Strawberry, alongside hotels such as Admiral Hotel and Villa Copenhagen. You’ll be part of a wider hospitality family, with staff benefits according to your employment terms.

Let’s talk

We’d love to hear a little about you, what you enjoy and why you’d like to join Hobo. Tell us whether your interests lie on the floor, behind the bar or a bit of both, along with when you’re available to work.

If you have hospitality experience, tell us about it. If you don’t, tell us what makes you keen to get started.

The practical details

• 
Position: On-call waiter or bartender, with shifts agreed according to business needs and your availability.

• 
Start date: February 2027, with the exact date to be agreed.

• 
Location: Hobo Copenhagen, Helgolandsgade 3, 1653 Copenhagen V.

• 
Working hours: Morning, daytime and evening shifts, primarily at weekends. You should be available at least every other weekend,  and we’d love to hear if you’re keen to work more.

• 
Questions: Contact Gobo Hansen, F&B Manager, at gobo.hansen@hobohotel.dk.

• 
Application deadline: November 16th

We review applications and meet candidates on an ongoing basis, and positions may be filled before the application deadline.

Chef - full time

Bring your craft to the kitchen at Hobo Copenhagen

You care about good food, enjoy a busy service and know how much a kitchen depends on the people in it. Now you’re ready to help build something new.

We’re looking for chefs to join Hobo Copenhagen in full-time positions, with a primary focus on our evening à la carte restaurant. You’ll also contribute to the food offering in our all-day bar, working as part of one kitchen team.

Our restaurant offers dishes made for sharing, good ingredients and confident flavours. We’re looking for people who bring care to their cooking, ideas to the conversation and a willingness to support the team.

Good food starts with us

Together with the Head Chef and your kitchen colleagues, you’ll help build a modern kitchen culture where everyone feels welcome and respected. We value calm, clear communication, constructive feedback and helping each other through a busy service. Everyone should feel comfortable asking questions, sharing ideas and learning.

Your role will include:

• 
Preparing and cooking dishes with attention to flavour, seasoning and presentation, keeping quality consistent throughout service.

• 
Looking after your section, planning your preparation and keeping your station organised and ready for a busy evening.

• 
Contributing ideas as we develop dishes, seasonal menus and the everyday food offering across our restaurant and all-day bar.

• 
Working closely with the service team to find the right pace, communicate clearly and take care of dietary requirements.

• 
Making thoughtful use of ingredients, keeping track of stock and helping reduce food waste.

• 
Following food safety, hygiene and allergen procedures, including checks and documentation in e-smiley.

• 
Sharing knowledge, helping colleagues and leaving the kitchen ready for the next service.

What you bring

You have professional kitchen experience, preferably from a busy à la carte restaurant, and feel comfortable running your own section.

You enjoy cooking food that people want to gather around. You’re attentive to the details, curious about ingredients and techniques, and open to both sharing ideas and learning from others.

You take responsibility for your work and contribute to a supportive atmosphere. You listen, share your knowledge and treat colleagues with respect, whatever their role or experience. When the pace picks up, you communicate clearly and work with the team to find solutions.

Relevant culinary training is welcome, and we also value strong practical experience. You can communicate confidently in English and are comfortable working evenings and weekends.

What you’ll be part of

At Hobo, we bring a professional, passionate and playful approach to hospitality. We want that to be felt in the kitchen as well as in the guest experience.

You’ll join during the opening journey, with the opportunity to contribute to menus, routines and team culture from the beginning. You’ll work closely with the Head Chef and a team that values good food, clear communication and room to develop.

Hobo Copenhagen is part of Strawberry, alongside hotels such as Admiral Hotel and Villa Copenhagen. We bring our own personality to that wider hospitality family, with access to development opportunities, staff hotel rates and food and beverage benefits.

Let’s talk

We’d love to hear about the person behind the CV. Tell us where you’ve worked, what you enjoy cooking and what matters to you in a kitchen team.

The practical details

• 
Position: Full-time chef.

• 
Start date: February 2027.

• 
Location: Hobo Copenhagen, Helgolandsgade 3, 1653 Copenhagen V.

• 
Working hours: Primarily afternoon and evening shifts, including weekends. Shifts typically start between 11:00 and 15:00 and finish between 22:00 and midnight, depending on the schedule.

• 
Questions: Contact Gobo Hansen, F&B Manager, at gobo.hansen@hobohotel.dk.

• 
Application deadline: November 16th

We review applications and meet candidates on an ongoing basis, and positions may be filled before the application deadline.

Bartender fulltime - Shape the bar at Hobo Copenhagen

You know your craft. You care about what goes into the glass, how a bar runs and how people feel when they walk through the door. You understand that a warm welcome, eye contact and genuine attention can set the tone for an entire evening. Now you’re ready to help build something new.

We’re looking for experienced bartenders to join Hobo Copenhagen in a full-time position, with a primary focus on our new cocktail bar. You’ll help develop a bar with its own identity, where cocktails, music and warm, confident hospitality come together.

Your craft. Your responsibility.

Help develop and refine our cocktail offering, contributing ideas, testing recipes and translating the concept into drinks that work consistently during service.

Take ownership of your shifts, from preparation and station setup to handovers and closing, keeping the team organised and the bar ready for the next service.

Work confidently with batching, dilution, temperature and presentation, understanding how preparation supports both quality and time with guests.

Maintain control of stock, rotation, waste and product quality, and contribute to ordering and stocktaking.

Share knowledge with colleagues and help strengthen beverage standards across our outlets.

The practical details

Position: Full-time bartender.

• 
Start date: February 2027.

• 
Location: Hobo Copenhagen, Helgolandsgade 3, 1653 Copenhagen V.

• 
Working hours: Varied shifts, including evenings, nights and weekends.

• 
Questions: Contact Gobo Hansen, F&B Manager, at gobo.hansen@hobohotel.dk.

Application deadline: November 16th

We review applications and meet candidates on an ongoing basis, and the position may be filled before the application deadline.

The practical details

Good food, good teamwork and the feeling of a service coming together. If you enjoy being part of a kitchen and want to keep learning, we’d love to meet you.

We’re looking for part-time chefs to join Hobo Copenhagen, supporting our evening à la carte restaurant and all-day bar. Our food centres on dishes made for sharing, good ingredients and confident flavours.

Rockwell Automation is a global technology leader focused on helping the world’s manufacturers be more productive, sustainable, and agile. With more than 28,000 employees who make the world better every day, we know we have something special. Behind our customers - amazing companies that help feed the world, provide life-saving medicine on a global scale, and focus on clean water and green mobility - our people are energized problem solvers that take pride in how the work we do changes the world for the better.

We welcome all makers, forward thinkers, and problem solvers who are looking for a place to do their best work. And if that’s you we would love to have you join us!

**Job Description

**As the Business Operations Program Manager you will be important member of the Global IPP Operations team and drive business productivity, process optimization, and organizational change projects across the IPP business. You will focus on improving end-to-end operational performance by implementing sustainable business improvements that enhance efficiency, collaboration, scalability, and customer responsiveness.

Acting as a strategic partner, you will support Project Management, Application Engineering, Manufacturing, and Business Operations teams. You will lead cross-functional initiatives that achieve four key objectives: simplifying processes, improving operational effectiveness, accelerating execution, and enabling business growth.

You will work closely with the Manufacturing teams in Katowice and CUBIC, ensuring strong alignment between operational improvement initiatives, production capabilities, and business objectives across the global IPP organization. You will combine data-driven decision-making, change management expertise, and continuous improvement methodologies to deliver measurable business outcomes and ensure successful adoption of transformational projects.

You will report to the Global IPP Business Operations Manager. This position is hybrid and located in EMEA, preferably near a Rockwell Automation IPP facility.

**Your Responsibilities

**

• 
Business Productivity and Process Improvement

• 
Lead business productivity projects across the IPP organization focused on improving efficiency and enhancing operational performance.

• 
Identify process bottlenecks and improvement opportunities across Project Management, Application Engineering, Manufacturing, and Business Operations.

• 
Develop and implement standardized processes, best practices, and governance mechanisms across the IPP business.

• 
Promote a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence across the organization.

• 
Change Management and Business Transformation

• 
Lead change management activities associated with strategic business initiatives, organizational transformations, system implementations, and process improvements.

• 
Partner with functional leaders to reinforce desired behaviors and ensure long-term adoption of new processes and tools.

• 
Establish change management methodologies, frameworks, and best practices within the IPP organization.

• 
Cross-Functional Business Integration

• 
Act as a liaison between Project Management, Application Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Operations, Commercial teams, and IPP Leadership.

• 
Drive alignment of priorities, processes, and performance goals across departments and regions.

• 
Support implementation of integrated business processes that enhance visibility and accountability

• 
Facilitate stakeholder alignment and resolution of process-related challenges impacting business performance.

• 
Performance Analytics and Operational Effectiveness

• 
Analyze operational trends to identify improvement opportunities and support data-driven decision-making.

• 
Monitor key metrics including productivity, lead time, OTTR, process adoption, and operational performance.

• 
Measure and communicate the impact of productivity and transformation programs.

• 
Support data governance efforts to improve visibility and reporting accuracy.

• 
Strategic Program Management

• 
Lead and coordinate productivity and transformation projects aligned with IPP strategic goals.

• 
Develop project charters, business cases, implementation roadmaps, and success metrics.

• 
Identify project risks, dependencies, and mitigation actions.

• 
Provide regular updates and recommendations to the IPP Leadership Team.

• 
Continuous Improvement

• 
Lead or support continuous improvement projects focused on operational productivity, process simplification, organizational effectiveness, and business performance.

• 
Identify opportunities to automate manual processes, improve reporting efficiency, and streamline workflows.

• 
Drive standardization of tools, methodologies, and governance processes across the IPP organization.

• 
Benchmark best practices and implement solutions that support long-term business growth.

**The Essentials - You Will Have

**

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Business Administration, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Organizational Development, or related field.

• Minimum 5+ years of experience in Change Management or Business Operations, Operational Excellence, Business Transformation, Project Management.

**The Preferred - You Might Also Have

**

• Experience working within Engineering-to-Order (ETO), manufacturing, industrial automation, or project-based business environments.

• Demonstrated experience leading business improvement and change management projects.

• Experience working within global and cross-functional organizations.

• Proficiency with business analytics tools.

• Strong change management and business process improvement skills.

• Strong understanding of project-driven and engineering-to-order business environments.

• Experience leading cross-functional programs in global organizations.

• Experience with data analytics & business performance measurement.

• Continuous improvement mindset with a passion for operational excellence.

**What We Offer

**Our benefits package includes …

• Volunteer Paid Time off available after 6 months of employment for eligible employees

• Company volunteer and donation matching program – Your volunteer hours or personal cash donations to an eligible charity can be matched with a charitable donation.

• On-demand digital course library for professional development

• Comprehensive mindfulness programs with a premium membership to Calm

• Employee Assistance Program

• Personalized wellbeing programs through our OnTrack program

• and other local benefits!

_At Rockwell Automation we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this or other roles.

_Rockwell Automation’s hybrid policy aligns that employees are expected to work at a Rockwell location at least Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays unless they have a business obligation out of the office.

jobs.description:
About the job

Are you looking for an active job where the days fly by and teamwork makes a real difference? We are currently looking for motivated and reliable employees to join Schou Company for both short-term and long-term temporary assignments, start up from December.

If you enjoy staying active, working with great colleagues, and being part of a fast-paced warehouse environment, this could be the perfect opportunity for you.

Your work assignments will be

• Manual unloading of containers

• Sorting and stacking goods onto pallets

• Preparing products for warehouse handling

• Working closely with colleagues to ensure daily targets are met

• Maintaining a safe and organized work area

Working Hours

Monday - Thursday: 06:00 - 15:00

Friday: 06:00 - 11:15

Salary

DKK 173.00 per hour + 10% in Fritvalg.

What Makes This a Great Place to Work?

At Schou Company, you will become part of a team where collaboration, respect, and a positive attitude are highly valued. New employees are welcomed into a supportive environment where colleagues help each other and work together to achieve common goals.

You will join a workplace that offers:

• A friendly and welcoming team

• A positive and supportive work environment

• Strong teamwork and collaboration throughout the day

• An international workplace with colleagues from different backgrounds

• A structured introduction and support from experienced team members

• Early finish every Friday, giving you a head start on the weekend

Who Are We Looking For?

We are looking for people who:

• Enjoy physical and active work

• Are reliable and punctual

• Can start work from December full time

• Have a positive attitude and strong work ethic

• Work well both independently and as part of a team

• Are comfortable with heavy lifting and physically demanding tasks

Please note that this is a physically demanding position. You will be on your feet throughout the day, and heavy lifting is a natural part of the job.

Language Requirements

You must be able to communicate in either:

• Danish or English

Start Date

As soon as possible

If you are ready to join a hardworking team and enjoy an active workday in a positive warehouse environment, we would love to hear from you. Candidates will be interviewed on an ongoing basis

Apply today and start your next opportunity with Schou Company.

**Job Description

**The Sales Manager & Strategic Account Lead is a pivotal leadership role combining people leadership, commercial execution, strategic account management, and customer engagement.

This role is responsible for building and developing a high-performing field team and for strengthening engagement across general practice, hospitals, pharmacies, and other relevant healthcare stakeholders and partners.

In parallel, the role serves as a strategic lead for Primary Care business and partnerships, with responsibility for improving patient care pathways through high-level stakeholder engagement, developing innovative partnerships, and driving customer segmentation and targeting excellence to optimize commercial execution and customer engagement.

The successful candidate will combine strong commercial capabilities with an entrepreneurial mindset, a passion for developing people, and the ability to translate strategy and customer insights into impactful execution.

**Key Responsibilities

**Sales Team Leadership

• Build, lead, coach, and inspire a high-performing field team to achieve commercial objectives across hospital, general practice, pharmacy channels, and strategic partnerships.

• Set clear priorities, performance expectations, and development goals to support individual and team success.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, innovation, and compliance.

Strategy Development and Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Partner closely with the Business Unit Lead, Marketing, and other cross-functional colleagues to shape commercial strategies and co-create solutions.

• Ensure that field execution and account management support overarching business and brand objectives.

• Act as a strategic bridge between field execution, Marketing, Market Access, Medical Affairs, Business Intelligence, Analytics, and other relevant functions.

Customer Segmentation & Targeting Excellence

• Lead the development, implementation, and continuous optimization of customer segmentation and targeting models.

• Ensure segmentation insights drive customer engagement strategies, account prioritization, resource allocation, omnichannel execution, and field force effectiveness.

• Translate customer, market, and behavioral data into actionable engagement frameworks.

Strategic Primary Care Engagement

• Strengthen engagement within Primary Care by building strategic relationships with key healthcare stakeholders and decision-makers.

• Identify opportunities to optimize and improve patient care pathways.

• Represent the organization in relevant healthcare forums and stakeholder engagements.

Partnership & Business Development

• Provide strategic direction and leadership in developing innovative commercial partnerships and new ways of engaging healthcare and non-traditional stakeholders.

• Identify and assess new opportunities and collaboration models that can improve customer engagement, patient pathways, and access to appropriate healthcare interventions.

• Support the development of scalable business cases and commercial models, including implementation coaching.

**Primary Tasks

**Sales & People Management

• Build and develop a strong field organization.

• Coach and develop team members to enable both individual and team success.

• Analyze territory data, customer engagement metrics, and market dynamics to optimize resource allocation, targeting, and commercial performance.

• Continuously refine customer segmentation and targeting models to optimize call planning, account prioritization, and customer engagement.

Strategic Commercial Alignment

• Collaborate with Marketing and cross-functional partners to provide field-based insights that shape go-to-market strategies.

• Drive adoption of segmentation-driven and omnichannel engagement approaches across the field organization.

• Ensure field execution remains closely aligned with business priorities.

Strategic Account Management

• Identify, map, prioritize, and engage critical stakeholders influencing Primary Care and patient pathways.

• Build strategic relationships with relevant healthcare decision-makers at local and regional levels.

• Identify friction points and opportunities within patient pathways and collaborate on solutions to improve patient outcomes.

Business Development & Partnerships

• Further develop strategic approaches to partnerships across traditional and non-traditional healthcare stakeholders.

• Prioritize partnership opportunities based on market insights, customer needs, and business potential.

• Support implementation of partnership models and commercial initiatives.

**Qualifications & Competencies

**Education

• Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Life Sciences, Public Health, or a related field.

**Experience

**

• Strong experience from the pharmaceutical, healthcare, or another relevant commercial environment.

• Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into impactful execution.

• Previous people leadership or Sales Manager experience is preferred but not required.

• Experience in Key Account Management, strategic account management, commercial excellence, sales force effectiveness, customer engagement, or similar commercially focused roles is an advantage.

• Experience using customer segmentation, targeting, customer insights, and analytics to improve commercial execution is preferred.

Leadership & People Development

• A people-oriented leader who can inspire, coach, and develop others.

• Ability to lead through collaboration, influence, accountability, and a genuine desire to enable others to succeed.

Market Knowledge

• Strong understanding of the Danish healthcare environment and the interaction between Primary Care, pharmacies, scientific leaders, healthcare decision-makers, and other relevant stakeholders.

Commercial & Strategic Acumen

• Strong strategic and entrepreneurial mindset.

• Ability to translate customer needs, market dynamics, data, and commercial opportunities into clear priorities and effective execution.

Data & Customer Insights

• Strong interest in using data and customer insights to inform decision-making.

• Ability to apply segmentation, targeting, account prioritization, and resource allocation principles effectively.

Communication & Influence

• Excellent interpersonal and presentation skills.

• Ability to build trust, create alignment, and influence colleagues and external stakeholders across functions and organizational levels.

Language

• Native or fluent Danish and professional fluency in English, both written and spoken.

**What We Offer

**

• A high-impact leadership role with broad commercial and strategic responsibility.

• The opportunity to shape customer engagement, strategic partnerships, and patient pathway improvements.

• A dynamic, collaborative, and cross-functional working environment.

• Significant opportunity to influence business strategy and execution.

• A role with strong focus on leadership development, innovation, and commercial excellence.

• The chance to work with talented colleagues and external stakeholders to create meaningful impact for patients and healthcare systems.
